split: Seed-42 random 80/20 train/test split; shuffle the 80% partition into five seed-42 folds; each fitted fold model is evaluated on the same test partition.
selection: The published search first evaluated a default, then requested up to 30 Optuna trials for CatBoost/XGBoost and 10 for TabNet, selecting by mean validation loss across the five folds. CatBoost/XGBoost were then refit at learning rate 0.015 with at most 20,000 trees and validation-based early stopping; that refit does not apply to TabNet. A 32-hour Optuna timeout made realized complete-candidate counts dataset/method dependent: RF1 and SCM20D each had CatBoost=31, XGBoost=31, TabNet=11 including the default; MoA had CatBoost=10, XGBoost=31, TabNet=10. SketchBoost inherited CatBoost's selected structural parameters and used the same lower-learning-rate refit. Its reduced-dimension strategy summaries sort candidate dimensions by mean test loss, so those strategy headline values are test-selected; the full-output and baseline rows do not have that dimension-selection leak. The clean fixed MBTR comparison instead caps each standard and linear-response fit independently at 1,000 trees with learning rate 0.05 and patience 50 on the held-out training fold, retains its validation-best iteration, freezes the model, and evaluates the common test set once.
aggregation: Mean and sample standard deviation over the five fitted fold models; this is not outer cross-validation.

split: Pinned SketchBoost Extreme Classification Repository train/test indices (first of ten predefined split columns); shuffle the training partition into five seed-42 folds; each fitted fold model is evaluated on the same fixed test partition.

split: Historical paper protocol: RF1 uses a chronological 4108/5017 split and SCM20D uses a fixed 7463/1503 split.
selection: Follow the paper's method-specific settings; use only as historical context for new experiments.
aggregation: Paper values were printed as aRRMSE multiplied by 100; catalog values are divided by 100.

selection: Method-specific published settings; rounded table values are protocol references rather than regression-test thresholds.
aggregation: One published value per method and dataset rounded to three decimals.

split: Use the downloaded KDIS iterative-stratified five-fold partitions exactly and record the archive checksum. Expand the dataset list only through a separately reviewed dense-subset manifest.
selection: The current KDIS artifacts contain only outer train/test folds, so the validation-early-stopped MBTR protocol is not applicable. The outer test fold must not select an iteration, threshold, feature set, or hyperparameter. A fixed-tree diagnostic must disable early stopping explicitly and be labelled separately. Any validation-based early stopping or tuning requires a reproducible inner split inside each outer training fold and defines a distinct nested protocol; the fixed 0.5 label threshold remains part of this catalog protocol.
aggregation: Report every outer fold plus mean and sample standard deviation. This fixed KDIS archive protocol is not the UCO 2024 comparison protocol, which uses ten supplied train/generalization partitions.

split: Reproduce the pinned upstream seeded splitter. Map run_id to source_seed=2000+run_id. Start from train/validation/calibration/test ratios 0.4/0.1/0.3/0.2; cap calibration at 2048 rows; distribute calibration excess equally over the other non-empty partitions; truncate sizes to integers and assign the remainder to test; then use torch random_split with the source seed. Persist the generated row indices. Preserve the upstream seed-dependent subsampling cap when reproducing its corpus.
preprocessing: Fit the upstream standardization of X and Y on training rows only. Train the matching standardized-target study and inverse-transform predictions for raw-unit metrics; label both scales explicitly.
selection: Select point-prediction hyperparameters and boosting iterations on validation rows only. For the fixed MBTR comparison, cap each standard and linear-response fit independently at 1,000 trees with learning rate 0.05 and patience 50, retain its validation-best iteration, freeze it, and evaluate test rows once. Leave calibration rows unused for point prediction and fit shared MBTR plus independent and external baselines on identical persisted indices.
aggregation: Report every run ID plus mean and standard deviation over run IDs 0-9 (source seeds 2000-2009). The paper's conformal coverage and region-size scores are not point-prediction baselines.
